en.activity: HP Inc. provides personal computing, printing, 3D printing, hybrid work, gaming, and other related technologies in the United States and internationally. The company operates through three segments: Personal Systems, Printing, and Corporate Investments.
en.products: HP Inc. provides personal computing, printing, 3D printing, hybrid work, gaming, and other related technologies in the United States and internationally.
en.customers: The Personal Systems segment offers commercial and consumer desktops and notebooks, workstations, thin clients, retail point-of-sale systems, displays, software, hybrid systems, and endpoint security and services, as well as lifecycle services, including support and deployment, configurations, and extended warranty services.
en.edge: HP Inc. was founded in 1939 and is headquartered in Palo Alto, California.

en.positioning: HP Inc. provides personal computing, printing, 3D printing, hybrid work, gaming, and other related technologies in the United States and internationally. The company operates through three segments: Personal Systems, Printing, and Corporate Investments.

The company operates through three segments: Personal Systems, Printing, and Corporate Investments. The Personal Systems segment offers commercial and consumer desktops and notebooks, workstations, thin clients, retail point-of-sale systems, displays, software, hybrid systems, and endpoint security and services, as well as lifecycle services, including support and deployment, configurations, and extended warranty services.
en.moat: HP Inc. benefits from its established presence in Computer Hardware and brand recognition.
en.risks: As a Computer Hardware company, HP Inc. is exposed to competitive pressure, regulatory changes in its operating regions, macroeconomic cycles, and shifts in consumer or enterprise demand affecting its core segments.
